text.House Cat: Visit a player and lay an egg in their nest. Learn their role and who they visited.
text.Goose: In the round the Goose is revealed, winners are losers and losers are winners during scoring. Visit a player: lay an egg in their nest and both their neighbours' nests.
text.Pelican: Visit a player. All players that visit you visit that player instead. Lay an egg for every redirected visitor. The player you visit is never redirected, even if they visit you.
text.Maine Coon: Visit a player. During the day, before anyone has called CAW CAW, you may stand up, bet any number of cards from your nest, and guess each player's animal. If you are correct, you win exclusively. Otherwise, you lose exclusively.
text.Lyrebird: Visit a player. Lay eggs in your nest equal to the number of eggs laid in their nest tonight.
text.Cassowary: Visit a player at night. If any eggs were laid in their nest tonight, kill them.
text.Brumby: Visit a player. Roles will rotate clockwise equal to the number of eggs laid in their nest tonight.
text.Ugly Duckling: You appear as Meowfia to investigators. Visit a player and steal the eggs laid in their nest tonight: those eggs come to your nest instead.
text.Top Cat: Visit a player and swap sides with them: if they are Farm, they become Meowfia and you become Farm. If they are already Meowfia, nothing happens.

notes: A dead player can still be eggsecuted. The round is then scored on that player's side as usual.
Everyone draws 2 cards at setup, before the night. Compare nests with their size after that draw: only the change overnight is evidence.
Animals and sides are dealt afresh every round. What a player was last round says nothing about this round.

review.headline: Swaps flipped a team every round, and honest confessions won two of the three
review.summary: This game ran on alignment swaps. Every round a Top Cat or a Switcheroo turned a player to the other side overnight. In round 1 Alex told the truth about his Top Cat swap, but the table did the egg math wrong and eggsecuted him. That handed dead Casey 10 points and a lead she never lost. In rounds 2 and 3 the swapped player confessed, the table believed them, and Farm won easily. Ellis's lies went unpunished in the talk, but he finished on 5 after throwing at his own teammate in round 3.

rounds.recap: Alex's Top Cat swapped him with Casey, so Casey became the Meowfia Lorikeet. Five visitors got Winks, and Alex winked Casey dead in beat 1. Alex confessed the swap truthfully. Blair and Ellis then argued that Casey's 'fourth egg' needed a House Cat, but that egg was Casey's own Lorikeet egg. The table voted out Alex, who was Farm, by 6 votes to 4, and dead Casey banked 10.

Blair's Top Cat swapped with Drew, making Drew the Meowfia Turkey. Blair confessed at once. All the egg counts fit (Mosquito plus Turkey on Alex, House Cat plus Turkey on Blair, Turkey on Finley). Drew's attack on Finley's bad Lorikeet reasoning was not enough, and Drew went out with 8 votes. Four Farm players banked 15 to 20 each.

Blair's Switcheroo swapped animals between Blair and Finley, so Blair became the Meowfia House Cat. Finley confessed the whole chain. Ellis, the real Top Cat, falsely claimed a Pigeon egg on Blair. Blair rightly pointed out that the two egg claims can't both be true. The table still chose Blair, Alex's Wink confirmed it, and everyone threw at Blair. That included Ellis, who believed his teammate was Farm.

highlights.text: Alex winks Casey in beat 1, then truthfully confesses he was the Top Cat who made her Meowfia. Wrong egg math gets him eggsecuted anyway, and dead Casey scores 10.
Ellis claims to be a Pigeon while saying 'Blair, you're the Top Cat and you visited Drew'. Only a House Cat could know that, and nobody noticed.
Freshly flipped Blair makes the sharpest point of the day: Ellis and Finley can't both have laid Blair's single egg. Blair uses it to defend Ellis's lie and frame the honest Finley.
Ellis, Meowfia, throws a 12 and a 13 at his own teammate Blair, thinking Blair is Farm. He gets no consolation and finishes on 5.

confusions.what: Said Casey's fourth egg needed a House Cat. Casey, as Lorikeet, laid her own egg by visiting Drew, who held a Wink. Blair built a wrong case against Alex on this.

Called the fourth egg 'odd' and threw at Alex. Did not see that the Lorikeet egg explained it.
Said his +1 egg as Lorikeet meant Drew held a Wink. The egg was the Turkey's, and Drew had no Wink. Finley had to take it back.
Said Alex and Blair visited him. Left out Finley, who also visited and got a Turkey egg.
Thought Blair was Farm and Finley Meowfia (he rated Finley 90%), even though Finley publicly confessed the Switcheroo swap. Threw at his own teammate and lost the consolation card.
Said 'I visited nobody important' as Wasp. The Wasp has no night visit.

review.title: Swaps and Confessions
problems: Side swaps decided every round. Top Cat appeared in all three rounds. Each time the holder ended up Farm and won by telling the truth, so Top Cat plays like a Farm card. The new Meowfia learns their side at dawn with no cover story ready. Round 3's Switcheroo flip worked the same way. Consider giving the flipped player some help, or making Top Cat cost the user something.

Winks were a strong private oracle. Winking someone on the other side draws 2 eggs, so Alex knew Casey's and Blair's sides for certain. Nest sizes are only listed at dawn, so he could not prove it. In round 1 the Lorikeet handed out five Winks, and the instant kill silenced Casey, the only player who could explain the egg count.

The public list of overnight changes cancels Mosquito confusion. Alex just read his true +2 from the Storyteller. If confusion is meant to matter, hide the per-nest changes or the confused player's line.

No flowers came up in 9 revealed cards, and nobody ever bet on Nobody, since every round had Meowfia. This game tested neither system. Magpie and Ugly Duckling did little, apart from Blair's +3 in round 1.

Throws were flat: nearly everyone threw their two highest cards at the consensus target. The one big swing came from round 1's wrong vote, which made a dead Casey the eventual winner. Allowing larger throws, or rewarding a lone correct dissent, could create more betting tension.
